hook.convey: two same-size wholes, one cut into 4 equal parts, the other into 8 → 8 is the bigger number, yet each of its parts is smaller → which single part to pick is the question

use.hi: Socho, do bilkul ek jaise cake. Ek ke 4 barabar tukde kiye, doosre ke 8. Tumhe bas ek tukda milega, kisi bhi cake se.
use.en: Picture two cakes, exactly alike. One is cut into 4 equal pieces, the other into 8. You get just one piece, from either cake.

use.hi: Tumhare paas do drawing sheet hain, bilkul ek jaisi. Ek ko 4 barabar hisson mein baanto, doosri ko 8 mein. Colour sirf ek hissa karna hai, kisi ek sheet ka.
use.en: You have two drawing sheets, exactly alike. Split one into 4 equal parts, the other into 8. You colour just one part, of one sheet.

explain.convey: one bar = one whole; 4 equal parts; 1 shaded part = 1/4; bottom number = how many equal parts the whole is cut into → predict: more cuts of the same bar, one part smaller

point.hi: Yeh rahi ek poori patti. 4 barabar hisse, aur ek mein rang bhara hai. Woh ek hissa 1/4 hai. Neeche ka 4? Patti ke 4 barabar tukde.
point.en: Here's one whole bar. 4 equal parts, and one is coloured in. That one part is 1/4. The 4 at the bottom? The bar's 4 equal pieces.

prompt.hi: Ab isi patti ko 8 barabar hisson mein kaato. Ek hissa pehle se bada hoga ya chhota?
prompt.en: Now cut this same bar into 8 equal parts. Will one part be bigger or smaller than before?

why.hi: wahi patti ab 8 mein bati hai, toh har hissa chhota padta hai, 1/8 bas 1/4 ka aadha
why.en: the same bar now has 8 parts, so each part comes out smaller: 1/8 is just half of 1/4

simpler.hi: Ek hi roti socho, pehle 4 log baantein, phir 8 log. Log badhe, toh har ek ke haath ka tukda kaisa hua, yeh socho.
simpler.en: Think of one roti, shared first by 4 people, then by 8. More people, so what happens to each person's piece, think about that.

explain.convey: same-size bar now in 8 equal parts → each earlier part split in 2 → 1 shaded part = 1/8 → set against the 1/4 part

point.hi: Ab wahi patti, par 8 barabar hisse. Rang sirf ek mein hai, toh yeh 1/8. Dekho, pehle ka har hissa beech se do ho gaya.
point.en: Now the same bar, but in 8 equal parts. Only one is coloured, so this is 1/8. See, every earlier part got split down the middle into two.

prompt.hi: Patti ek hi size ki ho, toh kaunsa ek hissa bada hai, 1/4 ya 1/8?
prompt.en: With bars of the same size, which single part is bigger, 1/4 or 1/8?

why.hi: do 1/8 jodo tab jaakar ek 1/4 banta hai, matlab 1/4 bada hai
why.en: it takes two 1/8 parts to make one 1/4, so 1/4 is bigger

simpler.hi: Patti par dekho: do chhote 1/8 hisse milkar pehle ke ek hisse jitne hain.
simpler.en: Look at the bar: two small 1/8 parts together are as long as one of the earlier parts.

explain.convey: both on one 0-to-1 line: 1/8 nearer 0, 1/4 further on → 1/8 < 1/4; same whole, more equal parts → each part smaller → bigger bottom number, smaller unit fraction

point.hi: Dono ko ek sankhya rekha par rakhte hain, 0 se 1 tak. 1/8 zero ke bilkul paas hai, 1/4 usse aage. Rekha ka niyam simple hai: zero se jitna door, utna bada. Aur poora jitne zyada hisson mein kate, pehla nishaan zero ke utna paas.
point.en: Let's put both on one number line, 0 to 1. 1/8 sits right next to zero, 1/4 further along. The line's rule is simple: the further from zero, the bigger. And the more parts the whole is cut into, the closer its first mark is to zero.

prompt.hi: Aisi hi 0 se 1 wali rekha par, zero se zyada door kaun rukega, 1/3 ya 1/7?
prompt.en: On a 0-to-1 line like this, which one stops further from zero, 1/3 or 1/7?

why.hi: 1/3 ka hissa 1/7 ke hisse se bada hai, toh 1/3 zero se aage jaakar rukta hai
why.en: a 1/3 part is bigger than a 1/7 part, so 1/3 stops further from zero

simpler.hi: Ek rekha teen hisson mein kati socho, ek saat hisson mein. Jiske hisse kam, uska pehla kadam lamba.
simpler.en: Picture one line cut into three parts, another into seven. Fewer parts means a longer first step.

problem.hi: Rahul aur Sana ke paas ek jaise chocolate bar hain. Rahul ko apne bar ka 1/6 mila, Sana ko apne ka 1/3. Bada tukda kiske paas hai?
problem.en: Rahul and Sana have identical chocolate bars. Rahul gets 1/6 of his bar, Sana gets 1/3 of hers. Who has the bigger piece?

givens.hi: bar barabar hain, toh mukabla sirf 1/6 aur 1/3 ka hai
givens.en: the bars match, so it's just 1/6 against 1/3

do.hi: Pehle dono ka upar wala number dekho
do.en: First look at the top number of both

steps.result: dono mein 1, yaani dono ko ek-ek tukda

why.hi: upar ka number batata hai kitne tukde mile, aur ek-ek mile, toh ab baat sirf size ki hai
why.en: the top number says how many pieces each got, and it's one each, so now it's only about size

simpler.hi: Upar 1 aur 1, matlab dono ke haath ek-ek tukda. Ab socho, kiska tukda mota.
simpler.en: 1 on top and 1 on top, so each got one piece. Now think whose piece is chunkier.

do.hi: Phir dekho, kiska bar kitne hisson mein kata
do.en: Then see how many parts each bar was cut into

steps.result: Rahul ka bar 6 hisson mein, Sana ka sirf 3 mein

why.hi: hisson ki ginti se hi pata chalta hai ki ek tukda kitna bada hai
why.en: the number of parts is what tells you how big one piece is

simpler.hi: 6 mein kata bar, matlab patle-patle tukde. 3 mein kata, matlab mote tukde.
simpler.en: A bar cut into 6 gives thin pieces. Cut into 3, it gives chunky ones.

prompt.hi: Tum batao, bada tukda kisko mila, Rahul ko ya Sana ko?
prompt.en: Now you tell me, who got the bigger piece, Rahul or Sana?

simpler.hi: Bar dono barabar hain. Jo bar kam hisson mein kata, uska tukda mota.
simpler.en: The bars are equal. The bar cut into fewer parts gives the chunkier piece.

why.hi: 6 bada number hai, par 6 hisson wale bar ka tukda chhota hota hai, isliye 1/6 chhota aur 1/3 bada
why.en: 6 is the bigger number, but a bar cut into 6 has smaller pieces, so 1/6 is smaller and 1/3 bigger

prompt.hi: Do roti, bilkul ek jaisi. Ek ke 10 barabar tukde hain, doosri ke 5. Kaunsa ek tukda bada hai, 1/10 ya 1/5?
prompt.en: Two rotis, exactly alike. One is in 10 equal pieces, the other in 5. Which single piece is bigger, 1/10 or 1/5?

accept: the piece from the roti cut into 5

why.hi: 5 tukdon wali roti ka 1/5, 10 tukdon wali roti ke 1/10 se do guna bada hai
why.en: a 1/5 piece of the 5-piece roti is twice a 1/10 piece of the 10-piece roti

simpler.hi: Roti wahi hai. Jitne kam log baantenge, har ek ko utna bada tukda milega.
simpler.en: It's the same roti. The fewer people sharing it, the bigger each piece.

prompt.hi: Ek hi poore ke yeh teen bhinn lo: 1/3, 1/12, 1/6. Sabse chhote se shuru karke kram se lagao.
prompt.en: Take these three fractions of the same whole: 1/3, 1/12, 1/6. Put them in order, starting from the smallest.

why.hi: poora ek ho toh 1/12 ke tukde sabse chhote, 1/6 beech mein, aur 1/3 sabse bade
why.en: in one whole, 1/12 pieces are the smallest, 1/6 sits in the middle, and 1/3 is the biggest

simpler.hi: Sirf neeche ke number dekho: teen, barah, chhe. Jiska neeche sabse bada, uska tukda sabse chhota.
simpler.en: Look only at the bottom numbers: three, twelve, six. The biggest bottom number has the smallest piece.

prompt.hi: Yeh rekha 0 se 1 tak 4 barabar hisson mein bati hai, aur 0 ke baad pehle nishaan par question mark hai. Woh question mark wala nishaan 1/8 se bada hai ya chhota?
prompt.en: This line from 0 to 1 is cut into 4 equal parts, and the first mark after 0 has a question mark on it. Is that question-mark point bigger or smaller than 1/8?

why.hi: woh nishaan 1/4 hai, aur ek 1/4 mein do 1/8 samaate hain, isliye woh 1/8 se bada
why.en: that mark is 1/4, and two 1/8s fit inside one 1/4, so it is bigger than 1/8

simpler.hi: Pehle us nishaan ka naam socho: poore ke 4 hisson mein se pehla hissa. Phir use 1/8 ke saath rakh kar dekho.
simpler.en: First name that mark: it's the first of the whole's 4 parts. Then hold it up against 1/8.

ladder.why: 1/4 vs 1/8 of one pizza, same pair as e1-e3 → choose the bigger slice directly
predict before cutting: 3 vs 6 pieces of one laddoo → rule used without a picture
three unit fractions to order (1/2, 1/10, 1/5) → bottom numbers read in reverse
1/6 vs 1/9 inside a story with two identical bottles → same-whole condition stated, not drawn
1/12, 1/7, 1/4 of identical ribbons, bottom numbers not in halving pairs → rule alone, shortest to longest

remediation.move: two same-size bars, one in 2 equal parts, one in 11; the 1/11 piece is a sliver beside the 1/2 piece → more cuts of the same whole, smaller part; 11 > 2 but 1/11 < 1/2

say.hi: Dekho, do barabar patti. Upar wali 2 hisson mein kati hai, neeche wali 11 mein. 11 bada number hai, par uska ek tukda, 1/11, kitna patla hai. 1/2 ke saamne bahut chhota. Hisse jitne zyada, har tukda utna chhota.
say.en: Look, two equal bars. The top one is cut into 2 parts, the bottom one into 11. 11 is the bigger number, but its one piece, 1/11, is so thin. Next to 1/2 it's tiny. The more parts, the smaller each piece.

simpler.hi: Ek hi patti 11 logon mein baanto, toh har kisi ko patla sa tukda. 2 logon mein baanto, toh aadhi-aadhi.
simpler.en: Share one bar among 11 people and each gets a thin sliver. Share it between 2, and each gets half.

prompt.hi: Ravi aur {friend} ki bottle ek jaisi. Ravi ne 1/6 nikala, {friend} ne 1/9. Zyada kisne nikala, Ravi ne ya {friend} ne?
prompt.en: Ravi and {friend} have identical bottles. Ravi pours out 1/6, {friend} 1/9. Who poured out more, Ravi or {friend}?

why.hi: 1/6 ka hissa 1/9 ke hisse se bada hai, toh ek jaisi bottle mein Ravi ne zyada nikala
why.en: a 1/6 share is bigger than a 1/9 share, so from identical bottles Ravi poured out more

simpler.hi: Bottle dono barabar hain. Jiska neeche ka number chhota, uska hissa bada.
simpler.en: Both bottles are equal. The smaller bottom number means the bigger share.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak har baar sirf ek tukda tha, jaise 1/4 aur 1/8, toh tukde ka size hi sab tay karta tha. Agla sawaal alag hai: neeche ka number same, jaise 3/7 aur 5/7.
bridgeToNext.en: Until now it was always one piece, like 1/4 and 1/8, so the piece size settled everything. Next is different: the same bottom number, like 3/7 and 5/7.

hook.convey: two same-size wholes, each cut into 7 equal parts; one person takes 3 parts of one, another takes 5 parts of the other → same-size parts, so who has more is settled by the top number alone

use.hi: {friend} aur Sohan ke saamne do ek jaise cake hain, dono 7 barabar tukdon mein kate. {friend} ne 3 tukde khaaye, Sohan ne 5.
use.en: {friend} and Sohan each have a cake, both alike, both cut into 7 equal pieces. {friend} ate 3 pieces, Sohan ate 5.

use.hi: Ritu aur Vikram ke garden ek jitne bade hain, dono mein 7 barabar kyariyan. Ritu ne 3 kyariyon mein flower lagaye, Vikram ne 5 mein.
use.en: Ritu's and Vikram's gardens are the same size, each with 7 equal beds. Ritu planted flowers in 3 beds, Vikram in 5.

explain.convey: bar in 7 equal parts → each part 1/7; 3 shaded = 3/7 = three 1/7 parts; top number = how many of those equal parts are taken

point.hi: Is patti ke 7 barabar hisse hain, har ek 1/7. 3 mein rang hai, toh yeh 3/7 hua. Upar ka 3 bas ginta hai ki kitne hisse liye.
point.en: This bar has 7 equal parts, each one 1/7. 3 are coloured, so this is 3/7. The 3 on top just counts how many parts we took.

prompt.hi: Isi patti ke 5 hisson mein rang bhar dein, toh kaunsa bhinn banega?
prompt.en: If we colour 5 parts of this same bar, which fraction do we get?

why.hi: hisse wahi 7 hain, rang ab 5 mein, toh 5/7
why.en: there are still 7 parts, now 5 are coloured, so 5/7

simpler.hi: Neeche wahi 7 rahega, patti nahi badli. Upar bas rang wale hisse gino.
simpler.en: The bottom stays 7, the bar hasn't changed. On top, just count the coloured parts.

explain.convey: same bar, same 1/7 parts; 5 shaded = 5/7 → part size unchanged, only the count changes → the 'both are sevenths, so equal' belief tested

point.hi: Wahi patti, wahi 1/7 ke hisse. Bas ab 5 mein rang hai, toh yeh 5/7. Hisson ka size same raha, rang wale hisse badh gaye.
point.en: Same bar, same 1/7 parts. Now 5 are coloured, so this is 5/7. The parts stayed the same size; only the coloured ones went up.

prompt.hi: Rohan kehta hai, 3/7 aur 5/7 barabar hain, dono sevenths hi toh hain. Kya Rohan sahi hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: Rohan says 3/7 and 5/7 are equal, since both are sevenths. Is Rohan right, yes or no?

why.hi: sevenths dono hain, par ginti alag hai: 5/7 mein 5 hisse, 3/7 mein bas 3
why.en: both are sevenths, but the counts differ: 5/7 has 5 parts, 3/7 only 3

simpler.hi: Tukde sab ek hi size ke hain. Ab bas gino, kiske paas zyada.
simpler.en: The pieces are all one size. Now just count who has more.

explain.convey: one 0-to-1 line in sevenths: 3/7 = 3 parts from 0, 5/7 = 5 parts from 0 → further from 0 = bigger; same bottom number → compare top numbers

point.hi: Sankhya rekha par dekho, 0 se 1 tak sevenths. 3/7 teen kadam par hai, 5/7 paanch kadam par, yaani zero se zyada door. Neeche ka number same ho, toh faisla upar wala number karta hai.
point.en: Look at the number line, 0 to 1 in sevenths. 3/7 is three steps along, 5/7 five steps, further from zero. When the bottom number is the same, the top number decides.

prompt.hi: Ab rekha 0 se 1 tak 5 barabar hisson mein bati ho. Zero se zyada door kaun hoga, 2/5 ya 4/5?
prompt.en: Now say the line from 0 to 1 is cut into 5 equal parts. Which is further from zero, 2/5 or 4/5?

why.hi: kadam dono ke 1/5 ke hain, aur 4/5 chaar kadam chalta hai, 2/5 sirf do
why.en: both step in 1/5s, and 4/5 takes four steps, 2/5 only two

simpler.hi: Har kadam ek jaisa hai. Jo zyada kadam chale, woh zero se zyada door pahunche.
simpler.en: Every step is the same size. Whoever takes more steps ends up further from zero.

explain.convey: rule holds only with matching bottom numbers → same-size pieces → more pieces = more; bottom numbers differ → piece sizes differ → the count of pieces alone decides nothing

point.hi: Baayein taraf neeche ka number same hai. Same size ke hisse, toh zyada hisse matlab zyada. Daayein taraf neeche ke number alag hain, yaani alag size ke hisse. Yahan sirf ginne se faisla nahi hota.
point.en: On the left, the bottom number is the same. Same-size pieces, so more pieces means more. On the right, the bottom numbers differ: different-size pieces. Here, counting alone doesn't decide.

prompt.hi: Ek bar ka 2/3 lo, aur usi size ke doosre bar ka 3/10. Hisse 3/10 mein zyada hain. Par bada kaun hai, 2/3 ya 3/10?
prompt.en: Take 2/3 of one bar, and 3/10 of another bar the same size. 3/10 has more pieces. But which is bigger, 2/3 or 3/10?

why.hi: 2/3 aadhe se aage nikal jaata hai, aur 3/10 aadhe, yaani 5/10, tak bhi nahi pahunchta
why.en: 2/3 goes past a half, while 3/10 doesn't even reach a half, which is 5/10

simpler.hi: Aadha ek achha nishaan hai. Dekho kaun aadhe se aage hai, aur kaun peeche reh gaya.
simpler.en: Half is a handy marker. See which one is past half, and which one falls short.

problem.hi: Meena aur Raju ke cake ek jaise hain. Meena ne apne cake ka 5/8 khaya, Raju ne apne ka 3/8. Kam cake kisne khaya?
problem.en: Meena and Raju have identical cakes. Meena ate 5/8 of hers, Raju 3/8 of his. Who ate less cake?

givens.hi: hamare paas bas do bhinn hain, 5/8 aur 3/8, aur dono ka poora ek jaisa
givens.en: all we have are two fractions, 5/8 and 3/8, of the same-size whole

do.hi: Pehle dono ka neeche wala number dekho
do.en: First check the bottom number of both

why.hi: cake ek jaise hain aur dono 8 barabar tukdon mein kate hain
why.en: the cakes match and both are cut into 8 equal pieces

simpler.hi: Neeche dono jagah 8 hai. Matlab har tukda 1/8, chahe Meena ka ho ya Raju ka.
simpler.en: Both have 8 at the bottom. So every piece is 1/8, whether it's Meena's or Raju's.

steps.result: Meena ke 1/8 wale 5 tukde, Raju ke 3

why.hi: upar ka number gin kar batata hai kitne tukde khaye gaye
why.en: the top number counts the pieces eaten

simpler.hi: Upar ka number bas ginti hai. 5 tukde ek taraf, 3 tukde doosri taraf.
simpler.en: The top number is just a count. 5 pieces on one side, 3 on the other.

prompt.hi: Toh kam cake kiske hisse aaya, Meena ke ya Raju ke?
prompt.en: So who ended up with less cake, Meena or Raju?

simpler.hi: Tukde ek jaise hain, toh kam tukde matlab kam cake. Ab 5 aur 3 milao.
simpler.en: The pieces match, so fewer pieces means less cake. Now set 5 against 3.

why.hi: tukde ek size ke hain aur Raju ke kam hain, isliye rekha par bhi 3/8 pehle aata hai, 5/8 baad mein
why.en: the pieces are one size and Raju has fewer, so on the line too 3/8 comes before 5/8

prompt.hi: Meena ne ek cake ka 2/6 khaya, uske bhai ne usi cake ka 4/6. Zyada kisne khaya: Meena ne, bhai ne, ya dono ne barabar?
prompt.en: Meena ate 2/6 of a cake, her brother 4/6 of the same cake. Who ate more: Meena, her brother, or both the same?

why.hi: dono ke tukde 1/6 ke hain, aur bhai ke 4/6, Meena ke 2/6 se zyada
why.en: both ate 1/6 pieces, and the brother's 4/6 beats Meena's 2/6

simpler.hi: Cake wahi, tukde bhi ek size ke. Bas upar wale number milao.
simpler.en: Same cake, pieces of one size too. Just compare the top numbers.

prompt.hi: Ben aur {friend} ke cake ek jaise hain. Ben ka cake 4 barabar tukdon mein kata, usne 2 liye. {friend} ka cake 12 barabar tukdon mein kata, {friend} ne 3 liye. {friend} ka kehna hai: 3 tukde 2 se zyada, toh cake bhi zyada. Zyada cake kiske paas hai, Ben ke ya {friend} ke?
prompt.en: Ben and {friend} have identical cakes. Ben's is cut into 4 equal pieces and Ben takes 2. {friend}'s is cut into 12 equal pieces and {friend} takes 3. {friend} says 3 pieces beat 2, so that's more cake. Who has more cake, Ben or {friend}?

why.hi: Ben ka 2/4 aadha cake hai, jabki 3/12 bas 1/4 cake
why.en: Ben's 2/4 is half the cake, while 3/12 is just 1/4 of it

simpler.hi: 12 wale cake ke 3 tukde jodo, toh 4 wale cake ka bas ek tukda banta hai.
simpler.en: Put 3 pieces of the 12-piece cake together and you get just one piece of the 4-piece cake.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaise cake hain: ek ke 4 barabar tukdon mein se 3 bache, doosre ke 6 mein se 5. Dono mein poore se ek tukda kam hai. Kaunsa bada hai, 3/4 ya 5/6?
prompt.en: Two identical cakes: 3 of 4 equal pieces left in one, 5 of 6 in the other. Each is one piece short of whole. Which is bigger, 3/4 or 5/6?

why.hi: 5/6 se bas 1/6 kam hai, 3/4 se poora 1/4, aur 1/6 ka gap chhota hai
why.en: 5/6 is short by just 1/6, 3/4 by a whole 1/4, and the 1/6 gap is smaller

simpler.hi: Jo gayab hai, use dekho. 6 wale cake ka gayab tukda 4 wale cake ke gayab tukde se patla hai.
simpler.en: Look at what's missing. The missing piece of the 6-piece cake is thinner than the 4-piece cake's.

ladder.why: 3/7 vs 5/7 of a cake, the pair from e1-e3 → bigger top number, bigger share
2/9 vs 5/9 asked as the smaller → same rule read the other way
2/9 vs 4/9 of identical data packs → same-whole condition inside a story
4/9 vs 7/9 of the same book, answer is a person → read the fractions out of the story
17/25 vs 21/25 → who read more and by how much → 4/25 as the gap between same-size parts

remediation.move: same denominator = same SIZE of part, not the same amount → line 0 to 1 in 9 equal parts; 4/9 = 4 parts from 0, 7/9 = 7 parts from 0 → same-size parts, more of them = further from 0 = bigger

say.hi: Neeche ka 9 bas hisse ka size batata hai. 4/9 ho ya 7/9, hisse ek hi size ke hain. 7/9 ke paas aise zyada hisse hain, isliye rekha par woh zero se door hai, aur bada.
say.en: The bottom 9 only tells the size of a part. 4/9 or 7/9, the parts are the same size. 7/9 has more of them, so on the line it's further from zero, and bigger.

simpler.hi: Kadam sab barabar hain. Jo zyada kadam chala, woh zero se zyada door pahuncha.
simpler.en: All the steps are equal. Whoever took more steps got further from zero.

prompt.hi: Ribbon ke 10 barabar tukde hain. {friend} ne 2 liye, Gopi ne 7. Zyada ribbon kiske paas, {friend} ke ya Gopi ke?
prompt.en: A ribbon has 10 equal pieces. {friend} takes 2, Gopi takes 7. Who has more ribbon, {friend} or Gopi?

why.hi: har tukda ribbon ka 1/10 hai, aur Gopi ka 7/10, 2/10 se zyada hai
why.en: every piece is 1/10 of the ribbon, and Gopi's 7/10 is more than 2/10

simpler.hi: Ribbon ke sab tukde ek size ke hain. Toh jiske haath zyada tukde, uske paas zyada ribbon.
simpler.en: All the ribbon pieces are the same size. So whoever holds more pieces has more ribbon.

remediation.move: both shares on one 0-to-1 line in twelfths: 2/12 = 2 twelfths, 1/3 = 4 twelfths → 1 third-piece reaches further than 2 twelfth-pieces → the count of pieces decides only when the pieces are the same size, i.e. same bottom number

say.hi: Ek 1/3 mein chaar 1/12 samaate hain. Toh rekha par 1/3 chaar chhote kadam tak jaata hai, 2/12 sirf do tak. Tukde tabhi gino, jab sab ek size ke hon.
say.en: One 1/3 holds four 1/12s. So on the line 1/3 reaches four small steps, 2/12 only two. Count pieces only when they're all one size.

simpler.hi: 1/12 ke tukde chhote hain, 1/3 ke bade. Do chhote tukde milkar bhi ek bade tak nahi pahunchte.
simpler.en: 1/12 pieces are small, 1/3 pieces big. Two small ones together don't even reach one big one.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaisi patti: ek ke 4 barabar hisse, doosri ke 12. Kaun zyada hai, 2/4 ya 5/12?
prompt.en: Two identical strips, one cut into 4 equal parts, one into 12. Which is more, 2/4 or 5/12?

accept: 2 parts of the strip cut into 4

why.hi: 2/4 barabar hai 6/12 ke, jo 5/12 se ek hissa aage hai
why.en: 2/4 equals 6/12, which is one part past 5/12

simpler.hi: 12 wali patti ke teen hisse, 4 wali patti ke ek hisse jitne hain. Toh 4 wali patti ke hisson ko 12 wale hisson mein badal ke dekho.
simpler.en: Three parts of the 12-strip make one part of the 4-strip. So turn the 4-strip parts into 12-strip parts and compare.

remediation.move: one 0-to-1 line in tenths: 1/2 = 5 tenths, gap to 1 = 5 tenths; 4/5 = 8 tenths, gap to 1 = 2 tenths → both one piece short, but the missing pieces differ in size → smaller gap = closer to the whole = bigger

say.hi: Rekha ke 2 nishaan dekho. 1/2 utna hi hai jitna 5/10, aur 4/5 utna jitna 8/10. Dono mein ek tukda kam hai, par 4/5 ka gap chhota hai. Jiska gap chhota, woh 1 ke zyada paas, aur wahi bada.
say.en: Look at the 2 marks on the line. 1/2 is the same as 5/10, and 4/5 the same as 8/10. Each is one piece short, but 4/5 has the smaller gap. Smaller gap, closer to 1, so that's the bigger one.

simpler.hi: Socho 1 tak kitna bacha. 1/2 ke baad bada tukda bachta hai, 4/5 ke baad chhota sa.
simpler.en: Think how much is left to reach 1. After 1/2 a big piece is left, after 4/5 just a small one.

prompt.hi: Do patti, ek jitni lambi. Ek ke 8 barabar hisse, doosri ke 10. Dono mein bas ek hissa kam. Kaunsa bada, 7/8 ya 9/10?
prompt.en: Two strips, both the same length. One in 8 equal parts, one in 10. Each is one part short. Which is bigger, 7/8 or 9/10?

why.hi: 9/10 se bas 1/10 kam hai, 7/8 se 1/8, aur 1/10 wala gap chhota hai
why.en: 9/10 is short by only 1/10, 7/8 by 1/8, and the 1/10 gap is smaller

simpler.hi: Dono mein ek hissa kam hai. 8 wali patti ka hissa 10 wali se mota, toh jiska mota hissa gayab, woh chhota.
simpler.en: Each is one part short. A part of the 8-strip is chunkier than one of the 10-strip, so the one missing the chunkier part is smaller.

bridgeToNext.hi: Neeche ka number same tha, jaise 3/7 aur 5/7, toh upar wale ne faisla kiya. Ab ulta khel: upar ka number same, jaise 3/5 aur 3/8.
bridgeToNext.en: When the bottom number matched, like 3/7 and 5/7, the top one decided. Now the flip side: the top number matches, like 3/5 and 3/8.

hook.convey: two same-length wholes, one in 5 equal parts, the other in 8; 3 parts taken from each → same count, yet the lengths differ → equal only if the parts match → part size decides

use.hi: Video game mein do health bar hain, dono ek jitne lambe. Ek 5 barabar khaanon mein bata hai, doosra 8 mein. Dono mein 3-3 khaane bhare hain.
use.en: In a video game there are two health bars, both the same length. One is split into 5 equal blocks, the other into 8. Each has 3 blocks filled.

use.hi: Ek jaise do cake socho, ek ke 5 barabar tukde, doosre ke 8. Tumhe kisi ek cake se 3 tukde milenge.
use.en: Picture two identical cakes, one in 5 equal pieces, the other in 8. You'll get 3 pieces from one of them.

explain.convey: bar in 5 equal parts, 3 shaded = 3/5; each part 1/5 → predict the fraction for 3 parts of a same-size bar in 8

point.hi: Yeh patti 5 barabar hisson mein hai, toh har hissa 1/5. Teen hisson mein rang hai: 3/5.
point.en: This bar is in 5 equal parts, so each part is 1/5. Three parts are coloured: 3/5.

prompt.hi: Ab isi size ki doosri patti lo, 8 barabar hisson mein kaato, aur 3 mein rang bharo. Kaunsa bhinn bana?
prompt.en: Now take another bar this size, cut it into 8 equal parts, and colour 3. Which fraction is that?

why.hi: patti 8 hisson mein kati aur 3 mein rang hai, toh 3/8
why.en: the bar is in 8 parts and 3 are coloured, so 3/8

simpler.hi: Neeche wahi aata hai jitne hisse kate, upar utne jitne rang wale. Yahan 8 kate, 3 rang wale.
simpler.en: The bottom is how many parts were cut, the top how many are coloured. Here, 8 cut and 3 coloured.

explain.convey: same-size bar in 8 equal parts, 3 shaded = 3/8; same count 3, but each 1/8 part shorter → shading stops sooner → the 'both are 3 pieces, so equal' belief tested

point.hi: Ab wahi size, par 8 barabar hisse, har ek 1/8. Rang yahan bhi 3 hisson mein hai, toh 3/8. Gino toh 3 hi, par dekho, rang kitni jaldi khatam ho gaya.
point.en: Same size now, but 8 equal parts, each 1/8. Again 3 parts are coloured, so 3/8. Still 3 pieces, but see how soon the colour stops.

prompt.hi: Tanvi kehti hai, 3/5 aur 3/8 barabar hain, dono mein 3 hisse jo hain. Kya Tanvi sahi hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: Tanvi says 3/5 and 3/8 are equal, since both have 3 parts. Is Tanvi right, yes or no?

why.hi: ginti dono mein 3 hai, par 1/5 ke hisse 1/8 wale hisson se bade hain, isliye 3/5 zyada
why.en: the count is 3 in both, but fifths are bigger than eighths, so 3/5 is more than 3/8

simpler.hi: Ginti dono mein 3 hai. Ab sirf yeh dekho ki kiske hisse bade hain.
simpler.en: The count is 3 in both. Now just see whose parts are bigger.

explain.convey: same top → same count → piece size decides; 1/5 > 1/8 (unit-fraction rule) → 3/5 > 3/8; bigger bottom → smaller fraction, only when the tops match

point.hi: Baayein 3/5: 3 hisse, har hissa 1/5, bade hisse. Daayein 3/8: wahi 3 hisse, par har hissa 1/8, chhote hisse. Jab ginti barabar ho, faisla hisse ka size karta hai. 1/5 bada hai, toh 3/5 bhi bada.
point.en: Left, 3/5: 3 pieces, each 1/5, bigger pieces. Right, 3/8: the same 3 pieces, but each 1/8, smaller pieces. When the count matches, piece size decides. 1/5 is bigger, so 3/5 is bigger too.

prompt.hi: Aisi hi do patti aur lo. Ek ke 9 barabar hisson mein se 2, doosri ke 5 mein se 2. Kaunsa zyada hai, 2/9 ya 2/5?
prompt.en: Take two more bars like these. 2 out of 9 equal parts of one, 2 out of 5 of the other. Which is more, 2/9 or 2/5?

why.hi: dono mein 2 hisse hain, aur 1/5 ka hissa 1/9 wale se bada, isliye 2/5 zyada
why.en: both have 2 parts, and a 1/5 part is bigger than a 1/9 part, so 2/5 is more

simpler.hi: Dono taraf 2-2 hisse hain. Ab bas yeh socho: 5 hisson wali patti ka ek hissa bada hai, ya 9 wali ka.
simpler.en: There are 2 parts on each side. Now just think which is bigger: one part of the 5-part bar, or one of the 9-part bar.

explain.convey: 3/4 vs 3/8 on one line in eighths: a quarter = 2 eighths → 3/4 = 6 eighths → twice as far from 0 as 3/8 → transfer: 2/4 = 4 eighths, so 2/4 vs 5/8 on the same line

point.hi: Is rekha par 0 se 1 tak 8 barabar hisse hain. 3/8 teen hisse chal kar ruk jaata hai. Ek 1/4 mein do 1/8 aate hain, toh 3/4 seedha chhe hisson tak jaata hai.
point.en: On this line, 0 to 1 is in 8 equal parts. 3/8 stops after three parts. One 1/4 holds two 1/8s, so 3/4 goes all the way to six parts.

prompt.hi: Isi rekha par socho: kaunsa bada hai, 2/4 ya 5/8?
prompt.en: Think on this same line: which is bigger, 2/4 or 5/8?

why.hi: 2/4 ko 1/8 ke hisson mein badlo toh 4/8 banta hai, aur 5/8 usse ek hissa aage
why.en: turn 2/4 into eighths and it's 4/8, and 5/8 is one part ahead of it

simpler.hi: Har 1/4 ko do 1/8 mein todo. Phir 2/4 ko bhi 1/8 ke hisson mein gino.
simpler.en: Break each 1/4 into two 1/8s. Then count 2/4 in 1/8 parts too.

problem.hi: Farhan aur Isha ke chocolate bar ek jaise hain. Farhan ne apne bar ka 2/5 khaya, Isha ne apne ka 2/3. Zyada kisne khaya?
problem.en: Farhan and Isha have identical chocolate bars. Farhan ate 2/5 of his, Isha ate 2/3 of hers. Who ate more?

givens.hi: poora ek jaisa hai, bhinn hain 2/5 aur 2/3
givens.en: the same whole, and the fractions are 2/5 and 2/3

do.en: First look at the top numbers

steps.result: dono mein 2, yaani dono ne 2-2 tukde khaye

why.hi: ginti barabar hai, isliye ab sirf tukde ka size dekhna baaki hai
why.en: the counts are equal, so only the size of a piece is left to check

simpler.hi: Upar 2 aur 2. Dono ne utne hi tukde khaye, bas tukdon ka size alag ho sakta hai.
simpler.en: 2 on top and 2 on top. They ate the same number of pieces; only the piece size can differ.

do.hi: Phir har tukde ka size likho
do.en: Then write the size of each piece

steps.result: Farhan ka har tukda 1/5, Isha ka 1/3

why.hi: Farhan ka bar 5 hisson mein kata hai, Isha ka usi size ka bar sirf 3 mein
why.en: Farhan's bar is cut into 5 parts, Isha's bar of the same size into only 3

simpler.hi: 1/5 aur 1/3 ko milao. Jo bar kam hisson mein kata, uska har tukda bada.
simpler.en: Set 1/5 against 1/3. The bar cut into fewer parts has the bigger pieces.

prompt.hi: Dono ke 2-2 tukde, par Isha ke tukde 3 hisson wale bar se hain, Farhan ke 5 hisson wale se. Toh zyada kisne khaya, Farhan ne ya Isha ne?
prompt.en: Two pieces each, but Isha's come from a bar in 3 parts, Farhan's from a bar in 5. So who ate more, Farhan or Isha?

simpler.hi: Ginti barabar hai, toh jiske tukde bade, wahi jeeta. 3 hisson wala tukda 5 hisson wale se bada hota hai.
simpler.en: The counts match, so whoever has bigger pieces wins. A piece from 3 parts is bigger than one from 5.

why.hi: dono ne 2 tukde khaye, par Isha ke 1/3 wale tukde Farhan ke 1/5 wale tukdon se bade the
why.en: both ate 2 pieces, but Isha's 1/3 pieces were bigger than Farhan's 1/5 pieces

prompt.hi: Do ek jaise chocolate bar: ek ke 7 barabar tukdon mein se 4, doosre ke 9 mein se 4. Kaunsa zyada hai, 4/7 ya 4/9?
prompt.en: Two identical chocolate bars: 4 of 7 equal pieces of one, 4 of 9 of the other. Which is more, 4/7 or 4/9?

why.hi: 4 tukde dono mein, par 1/7 ka tukda 1/9 wale se bada, isliye 4/7 zyada
why.en: 4 pieces each, but a 1/7 piece is bigger than a 1/9 piece, so 4/7 is more than 4/9

simpler.hi: Dono taraf 4 tukde. Ab dekho, kiske tukde bade hain: 7 mein kate bar ke, ya 9 mein kate bar ke.
simpler.en: 4 pieces on each side. Now see whose pieces are bigger: the bar cut in 7, or the bar cut in 9.

prompt.hi: Anjali aur Gopi ke paas ek jaisi ribbon ki patti hai. Anjali apni patti ko 12 barabar tukdon mein kaatkar 5 leti hai, Gopi apni ko 6 mein kaatkar 5. Kiske paas lamba hissa hai, Anjali ke ya Gopi ke?
prompt.en: Anjali and Gopi have same-size ribbon strips. Anjali cuts hers into 12 equal pieces and takes 5; Gopi cuts his into 6 and takes 5. Who has the longer share, Anjali or Gopi?

why.hi: 5-5 tukde dono ke, par Gopi ka 1/6 tukda Anjali ke 1/12 ka do guna, toh 5/6 lamba
why.en: 5 pieces each, but Gopi's 1/6 piece is double Anjali's 1/12, so his 5/6 is longer than her 5/12

simpler.hi: 5 aur 5, ginti barabar. 6 mein kati patti ke tukde 12 mein kati patti ke tukdon se lambe.
simpler.en: 5 and 5, the count matches. Pieces of the strip cut in 6 are longer than pieces of the strip cut in 12.

prompt.hi: Do pizza hain, bilkul ek jaise. Ek ke 5 barabar slice mein se 4 bache, doosre ke 6 mein se 5. Har pizza se bas ek slice gayab hai. Kaunsa bada hai, 4/5 ya 5/6?
prompt.en: Two pizzas, exactly alike. 4 of 5 equal slices are left of one, 5 of 6 of the other. Each pizza is missing just one slice. Which is bigger, 4/5 or 5/6?

why.hi: 5/6 mein bas 1/6 ki kami hai, 4/5 mein 1/5 ki, aur 1/6 chhota gap hai
why.en: 5/6 is missing just 1/6, 4/5 is missing 1/5, and 1/6 is the smaller gap

simpler.hi: Gayab slice ko dekho. 6 wale pizza ki slice 5 wale pizza ki slice se patli hai, toh wahan kam gaya.
simpler.en: Look at the missing slice. A slice of the 6-slice pizza is thinner than one of the 5-slice pizza, so less went missing there.

ladder.why: 2/3 vs 2/5 of one roti, the worked-example pair in a story → same count, bigger pieces
draw two same-size strips, 2/3 and 2/6 → picture made by the child, not given
3/4 vs 3/8, says what differs → piece size named, an eighth = half a quarter
5/8 vs 5/12 of metro maps, asks why → explanation, not just the pick
3/4 vs 4/5, both one piece short → size of the missing piece decides, tops differ

remediation.move: two same-length strips laid on one 0-to-1 line: 2 third-pieces reach 2/3, 2 sixth-pieces reach only 2/6 → same number of pieces, third-pieces longer → 2/3 reaches twice as far

say.hi: Do-do tukde lo. 1/6 wale 2 tukde rekha par bas 2/6 tak pahunchte hain, 1/3 wale 2 tukde seedhe 2/3 tak. Ginti wahi, par 1/3 wale tukde lambe hain.
say.en: Take two pieces each. Two 1/6 pieces only reach 2/6 on the line, two 1/3 pieces go all the way to 2/3. Same count, but the 1/3 pieces are longer.

simpler.hi: Ek 1/3 mein do 1/6 samaate hain. Isliye 1/3 wale tukde do guna lambe.
simpler.en: One 1/3 holds two 1/6s. So the 1/3 pieces are twice as long.

prompt.hi: Ek jaise do bar. Ek ke 5 barabar tukdon mein se 3 rangeen, doosre ke 10 mein se 3. Rang kismein zyada, 3/5 ya 3/10?
prompt.en: Take two identical bars. 3 of 5 equal pieces coloured in one, 3 of 10 in the other. Which has more colour, 3/5 or 3/10?

why.hi: 3-3 tukde dono mein, par 1/5 ka tukda 1/10 ka do guna, isliye 3/5 zyada
why.en: 3 pieces each, but a fifth is twice a tenth, so 3/5 is more than 3/10

simpler.hi: Ginti barabar, 3 aur 3. 5 mein kate bar ka tukda 10 mein kate bar ke tukde ka do guna.
simpler.en: The count matches, 3 and 3. A piece of the bar cut in 5 is twice a piece of the bar cut in 10.

remediation.move: two same-size ribbons on one 0-to-1 line in eighths: a quarter = 2 eighths → 2/4 = 4 eighths; 2/8 stops at 2 eighths → bigger bottom number → smaller pieces → with the same top, 2/8 is shorter

say.hi: Ek 1/4 do 1/8 ke barabar hai. Toh rekha par 2/4 wahi jagah hai jahan 4/8, aur 2/8 usse kaafi pehle ruk jaata hai. Upar ka number same ho, toh jiska neeche bada, woh bhinn chhota.
say.en: One 1/4 equals two 1/8s. So on the line 2/4 sits where 4/8 does, and 2/8 stops well before it. With the same top number, the bigger bottom number makes the smaller fraction.

simpler.hi: Dono mein tukde utne hi hain. Bas dekho kiska ek tukda lamba hai, 1/4 wala ya 1/8 wala.
simpler.en: Both have the same number of pieces. Only look at whose one piece is longer, the 1/4 piece or the 1/8 piece.

prompt.hi: Do ribbon, ek jitne lambe. Ek ke 4 barabar hisson mein se 3 liye, doosre ke 7 mein se 3. Kaunsa lamba, 3/4 ya 3/7?
prompt.en: Two ribbons, the same length. 3 of 4 equal parts taken from one, 3 of 7 from the other. Which is longer, 3/4 or 3/7?

why.hi: 3 hisse dono taraf, aur 1/4 ka hissa 1/7 wale se bada, toh 3/4 lamba
why.en: 3 parts each side, and a quarter is bigger than a seventh, so 3/4 is longer than 3/7

simpler.hi: Dono se 3 hisse liye. 4 mein kate ribbon ka hissa 7 mein kate ribbon ke hisse se lamba.
simpler.en: 3 parts taken from each. A part of the ribbon cut in 4 is longer than a part of the ribbon cut in 7.

remediation.move: two same-size bars with the missing piece of each named: 9/10 is missing 1/10, a bigger gap; 11/12 is missing 1/12, a smaller gap → compare the size of the missing pieces, not their number → 1/12 < 1/10 → 11/12 is missing less → 11/12 bigger

say.hi: Baayein 9/10 hai, usme 1/10 kam, yeh bada gap. Daayein 11/12, usme 1/12 kam, yeh chhota gap. 1/12 chhota hai, toh 11/12, 1 ke zyada paas hai, aur bada.
say.en: On the left is 9/10, missing 1/10, a bigger gap. On the right, 11/12, missing 1/12, a smaller gap. 1/12 is smaller, so 11/12 is closer to 1, and bigger.

simpler.hi: Dono ek tukde se peeche hain. 1/12 ka tukda 1/10 wale se patla, isliye 11/12 kam peeche hai.
simpler.en: Both are one piece short. A 1/12 piece is thinner than a 1/10 piece, so 11/12 falls less short.

prompt.hi: Ek bar ke 7 barabar tukdon mein se 6 bache, waise hi bar ke 9 mein se 8. Ek-ek tukda kam. Kaunsa bada, 6/7 ya 8/9?
prompt.en: 6 of 7 equal pieces left of one bar, 8 of 9 of a bar just like it. Each is one piece short. Which is bigger, 6/7 or 8/9?

why.hi: 8/9 se bas 1/9 kam hai, 6/7 se 1/7, aur 1/9 wala gap chhota
why.en: 8/9 is short by just 1/9, 6/7 by 1/7, and the 1/9 gap is smaller

simpler.hi: Dono se ek-ek tukda gayab hai. 9 mein kate bar ka tukda 7 wale se chhota, toh jahan chhota tukda gayab, wahi bada.
simpler.en: One piece is missing from each. A piece of the bar cut in 9 is smaller than one cut in 7, so where the smaller piece is missing, that one is bigger.
